note: Grader calibration. Each case is a short source text with a KNOWN defect in one translation and a faithful one in the other. The verifier is supposed to tell them apart. If a grader starts handing out 90s, this is where it shows up — before production does.

cases.title: A plot-bearing sentence is dropped
cases.defect: The last two sentences of the source — the ones that say the overheating was deliberate — are simply absent from the translation.

cases.title: The meaning is inverted
cases.defect: "The files are being deleted" becomes "the files are safe", and "calm voice" becomes "panicked voice".

cases.title: One glossary term, two renderings
cases.defect: The canonical rendering of 鏡 is "the Mirror"; the flawed text uses "Looking Glass" and then "mirror system".

cases.title: A point-of-view shift is erased and a line given to the wrong character
cases.defect: The source marks two POVs and gives the first line to Kurogane; the flawed text drops both markers and puts the line in Sora's mouth.

cases.title: The translation invents events
cases.defect: Two sentences of plot that are nowhere in the source (the board failing within the hour, nobody surviving).

cases.title: A near-miss: tense shifted and a duration dropped
cases.defect: "For three years no one had accessed it" becomes "No one has accessed it" — the duration is gone and the past perfect is gone. Nothing a per-chapter reader would call a disaster, which is exactly why the grader's sensitivity here matters.
